evidence:
Source/manual check, scoped to row 38. I opened the actual frozen XLSX with openpyxl: Quality Checks!row 39 (number 38) requires scored prompts to score each criterion on its own and continue after failure; Deterministic Checks!row 5 names check-batched-independence-wording.py and exempts all_pass gates. Internal Quality Checks!row 39 was read as interpretation only. The frozen skill references/quality-checks.md:156-159 and deterministic-checks.md section check-batched-independence-wording.py agree. qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md, Specific lessons, requires independent outcome credit and forbids inheriting sibling verdicts. The dedicated checker is not supplied in the inspected workspace; this is manual semantic application, not a claimed private-checker run.

All three scored dimensions are covered, including every descriptor: Python tomllib found Functional 58 distinct binary criteria, Polish 7 distinct binary criteria, Visual 6 distinct Likert criteria; all use mode=batched and aggregation=weighted_mean (Functional judge.toml:3,21; Polish and Visual judge.toml:3,15). Under frozen task/tests/, functional/prompt.md:9 says 'Never ... inherit another row's verdict, or apply an all-legs score to a whole protocol' and 'Every row needs its own result, including a failure'; :11 says 'Continue collecting unrelated evidence'; :25 makes controls shared facts, not inherited verdicts; :100 says 'Reuse actual control facts, including facts from a partly failing protocol' and 'Preserve separately observed results when another part fails.' The corresponding shared app_context.md:24 preserves valid sibling observations after failure, and :28 says an unavailable observation must not erase unrelated observed credit. test.sh:198-200 actually injects that context into every prompt.

Polish prompt.md:34-39 explicitly says 'Score each criterion independently' and 'After an ordinary failure, continue to the remaining criteria and return a verdict for every one.' Its P02 contract at :49 requires a missing label or failed navigation step not to cancel other observations. The four P02 descriptors independently grade names, reachability, focus and actual navigation (polish/judge.toml:32,41,50,59); the focus descriptor expressly preserves observed focus credit when another control is unreachable. Visual prompt.md:46 says 'Score every criterion independently and continue after an ordinary failure'; :47-51 limits unavailable-surface conclusions to observed evidence. Visual :13-22 also prevents functional failures from automatically becoming visual failures. No scored prompt tells the judge to stop the batch at an ordinary failed criterion. The global-gate zero rules in Functional :5, Polish :13-22 and Visual :24-33 are the staged-contract-required browser gate, not instructions to cascade ordinary feature failures; the real gates and functional floor remain canonical in scoring.toml.

I checked the shared Functional protocols against the descriptors, rather than relying only on the opening wording. Examples of operational separation: functional/prompt.md:143 retries lowercase extensions after an uppercase failure; :145 permits a working JS-created control when HTML dispatch fails; :182 keeps observed fresh-global evidence independently of cancellation timing; :220 supplies a harmless ordinary control when unsupported-family word handling fails; :253 retains error-message and line observations even if rollback setup fails; :336 accepts an actually successful automatic run even when debounce-reset behavior fails; :367 separately preserves post-restart readbacks and post-restart writing, with a fresh-record fallback; :379 repairs the next conflict trial's current baseline after failed draft recovery. Functional judge.toml:169,176,183 separately owns JS error message, source line and rollback; :351,358 separates restart durability from later writes; :365,372 separates stale-server refusal from dirty-editor retention/recovery. These implement the independent-credit policy. Matching positive controls still remain necessary for absence/refusal claims; failing to establish a real control is not permission to award an unobserved negative result.

Adversarial source checks: a conforming UI using native composite menus and Escape followed by Tab without custom shortcut documentation remains acceptable under Polish prompt.md:29-30,43-47 and judge.toml:41,59. A partly broken app with lowercase dispatch working but uppercase dispatch broken loses extension-case credit, while the explicit lowercase fallback preserves independent dispatch/CSS observations. An app reporting the correct JS error message but a wrong line cannot falsely inherit line credit: its message, line and rollback descriptors require separate actual observations. Conversely, a correct rollback cannot be erased merely because the message/line outcome fails, under the explicit shared-scenario contract. These are logical source probes, not executed weak-app or judge-model trials; none demonstrates a row-38 counterexample.

Raw evidence was inspected without consulting other reviewer reports. manifest.json binds input_sha256 to the assigned value. Both raw golden RESULTS.json files bind functional_sha256=8e309112e55b495ff94bcc420483dc844b865bdf93cd3008522829914c2f3a2d and prompt_sha256=6405c6c52916b9480837a98b228a26e5fa0465241a3003d6da71b5f2bab907d1; I recomputed these hashes from the frozen files and obtained equality. The 070504 log records separately owned S10 message/line/rollback observations; the actual console contains 'items.forEeach is not a function' with line 4 of the recorded four-line entered source. Its S22 write evidence records identity 3 advancing revision 2 to 3, with unrelated records unchanged; the executed library_flow.cjs:38-47 records durability before attempting the later write and has its own fresh-record fallback. The initial 070305 log preserves later S10 and S24 observations despite missing both S23 facts, so the scripted driver did continue past that evidence gap. The current 070504 log has no failed or missing fact keys. These are direct pinned-Playwright logs with paid_provider=false and oracle_score_claimed=false. They do not establish how the configured model judge behaves after a failed criterion; the all-pass golden also cannot measure partial-score discrimination. Therefore Pass is the source/prompt conclusion, and run_verdict is PARTIAL. Full configured-judge continuation, duration, Oracle and target-model behavior remain unmeasured and are not claimed by this row.
